problem: Answering time-sensitive questions from long documents requires temporal reasoning over the times in questions and documents; it is open whether LLMs can do this from text alone or benefit from externally extracted temporal structure.
method: Use existing temporal information extraction systems to build temporal graphs of events, times and relations in questions and documents, then fuse these graphs into Transformer models for time-sensitive QA.
key_assumptions: Existing temporal information extraction systems can construct useful temporal graphs of questions and documents
Fusing temporal graphs into text input benefits Transformer reasoning
main_contribution: A method for fusing temporal graphs of events, times and temporal relations into Transformer input, establishing state-of-the-art performance on SituatedQA and three TimeQA splits.
baselines: Transformer models with and without fine-tuning
results: Fusing temporal graphs into input text substantially enhances temporal reasoning of Transformer models with or without fine-tuning and outperforms graph convolution-based approaches, setting new state-of-the-art performance on SituatedQA and three TimeQA splits.
limitations: Targets temporal reasoning over a given document set rather than selecting among document versions

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: Improves temporal reasoning inside the reader by injecting extracted temporal graphs, not by re-ranking retrieved passages by version time; no amended/versioned documents or validity intervals.
relation_to_idea.basis: Abstract shows temporal-graph fusion into Transformer encoders evaluated on SituatedQA/TimeQA; shares the time-sensitive QA problem and two relevant benchmarks but has no retrieval-ranking or document-version component.
